title: Introduce tenant location assertor and RBAC v2 decision cache
author: Aisha Martinez
release_notes: Add a location assertion step to RBAC v2 evaluations and a small in-memory decision cache to reduce policy evaluation latency; audit events are archived in a region-aware, signed store. No customer-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Some enterprise customers require strict per-request enforcement of data residency and KMS locality. Existing RBAC v2 evaluations computed policies and attribute checks on each request which increased p95 policy latencies and made per-request KMS-affinity checks expensive. This PR adds an explicit Location Assertor stage and a short-lived decision cache to reduce repeated policy work while preserving per-request residency guarantees.

What this PR does (high-level): Adds a small Location Assertor micro-component to the policy evaluation pipeline that: 1) resolves tenant geolocation claims (from tenant profile, VPC region, request headers) with precedence rules; 2) emits a signed "location-assertion" attribute used by RBAC v2 policy expressions for KMS region affinity; 3) records a compact audit envelope to the audit-proofs service. Introduces an in-process decision cache keyed by (tenant_id, route, assertion_hash, evaluation_version) that caches deterministic RBAC decisions for up to 30s to reduce repeated evaluation cost. Adds an Audit Archiver component that batches and signs audit envelopes and writes to the region-sticky immutable store with encryption context that includes the resolved location.

Design decisions and tradeoffs: The decision cache is intentionally conservative (short TTL, strict key includes evaluation_version) so that policy rollouts and canary changes don't create stale authorizations. Location resolution uses a deterministic precedence: explicit tenant override > VPC regional binding > request-region header. We do not trust free-form geo headers unless the tenant has "region_override" enabled. Audit envelopes are signed with the platform signing key and include a provenance bundle to support later attestation.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind flag "rbac.v2.location_assertor". Default off for all customers. Rollout sequence: 1) enable in staging and run integration tests (automated), 2) canary on 3% of traffic in prod for tenants with a residency requirement annotation, 3) measure policy p95 and audit throughput; 4) enable wider after 72h if no regressions. In the rare event of a problem the feature flag allows immediate kill-switch.

Testing and benchmarks: Unit+integration tests added for resolution precedence, cache eviction, and audit envelope signing. End-to-end performance tests on benchlab show median policy eval time reduced from 2.1ms -> 1.6ms for high-frequency tenant routes and p95 reduced ~12%. Decision cache hit-rate observed ~37% during synthetic steady-state workloads for common tenant routes.

Files touched (high level): src/policy/location_assertor.go, src/policy/decision_cache.go, src/policy/audit_archiver.go, pkg/config/feature_flags.go, api/docs/rbac_v2.md (note: docs update adds a small section describing the assertion attribute), bench/bench_policy_eval_test.go, infra/helm/templates/audit-archiver.yaml, internal/keys/signing_key_rotation.md.

Commits summary: 6 commits including initial implementation, unit tests, bench harness updates, docs, and a follow-up tightening of TTL logic after reviewer feedback.

Security and compliance notes: Audit envelopes include minimal tenant identifiers and are encrypted with CMK scoped to the resolved region. The archiver validates destination store region matches the resolved location or fails closed. All storage writes go through the CMK-scoped write path and are audited. This change required a minor addition to RBAC policy grammar to expose the attribute attribute::location_assertion (documented).

Compatibility / migration: No breaking API changes. Operators will need to opt-in via the feature flag and provide a signing key in the cluster secret for audit envelopes. The default behavior when the feature is off is identical to current RBAC v2 behavior.

Known limitations: Decision cache does not cover non-deterministic policies (policies using request timestamps or external lookups). Location resolution currently supports AWS/GCP/Azure region formats; adding custom provider mappings is tracked in ENG-3470.

Follow-ups: ENG-3470 - provider mapping table for custom region strings; ENG-3501 - persistent audit-proofs backfill for pre-assertion events.

review_thread: Evan Chu: Please describe how we avoid cache poisoning if a tenant's policy references non-deterministic external data.

Aisha Martinez: Good point — the cache only accepts decisions for policies annotated deterministic=true or for routes explicitly marked cachable. Non-deterministic policies bypass the cache (added tests).
Priya Raman: Audit store writes need stronger failure semantics. If the archiver fails to write because region mismatch, what happens?

Aisha Martinez: The archiver fails closed and the evaluation returns denied if audit archiving is mandatory for tenant. For non-mandatory tenants we implement a retry/backoff and emit a critical metric. Documented in security notes and added unit tests.
Marco Silva: Can we add a small e2e smoke test that ensures assertion is present in the final policy trace?
Aisha Martinez: Added an integration smoke test in tests/integration/test_location_assertor.yaml that validates assertion presence and signed envelope.
